finding: HNSW p50 latency is lower than exact for every valid paired configuration.
Recall@5 losses are small at higher ef and largest at ef=10, especially on 50k.
Recall and accuracy do not move monotonically together; classification differences are not significant after Holm.
Within each size, higher ef raises latency while improving or preserving Recall@5.
Latency advantage of HNSW is larger at 50k than 10k.
Index size is ~5 MB at 10k and ~25 MB at 50k; build time is paid once.
Controlled HNSW obtains index scans at 10k/ef=400 where natural planner falls back.
Exact is preferable when deterministic full recall and simplicity matter more than latency.
HNSW is preferable when warm-cache latency dominates and small recall losses are acceptable.
